what: Round 52 (owner): forced losses of Russian supply that are not Ukraine's strikes (those are strike_supply_r51.json), by cause, as [low, central, high]. Each cause lowers the no-war level of the buyers it fell on, as round 51 does for the strikes: shift = actual - (baseline - lost). Buyers under their own embargo for that product, and buyers a ban exempted, get nothing.
rule: A country's figure reflects its own choices and the foreseeable answers to them. Things forced on it that it did not choose - Ukraine's strikes on Russian refineries, Russia's sudden export bans - count neither for it nor against it.

export_ban_2023.what: Russia's ban on gasoline and diesel exports (Government decree No. 1537 of 21 September 2023); diesel by pipeline allowed again from 6 October, gasoline from 17 November 2023. Not in round 51 (it answered domestic prices, before the strike waves); round 51's 2023 strike loss is 0 (capped), so nothing is counted twice. The bans from March 2024 are in round 51 (through the strike pass-through) and not here.

source.name: Russia's 2023 gasoline and diesel export ban: decree No. 1537 (21 Sep 2023), exemptions and the export volumes lost (Reuters/LSEG, Bloomberg/Vortexa, Interfax, Enerdata)
source.note: the no-war level of buyers the ban cut off is lowered by the fuel it kept from them; see research/2026-10/gaps/forced_loss_r52-notes.md

druzhba_2026.what: The southern Druzhba pipeline to Hungary and Slovakia stopped from 27 January to 22 April 2026 after a Russian strike near Brody in Ukraine. Neither buyer chose it. Days of flow lost, on the buyer's own crude purchases that year, compared with the days the pipeline flowed.
druzhba_2026.not_counted: CZE (stopped Russian crude by its own choice in April 2025); POL and DEU (northern branch, stopped by choice in 2023); BLR (upstream of Brody).

source.name: Druzhba south halted 27 January - 23 April 2026 after a Russian strike near Brody (Slovak economy ministry, MOL, Ukraine's foreign ministry; via The Moscow Times, oenergetice.cz, intellinews)
source.note: Hungary's and Slovakia's no-war level of crude is lowered by the 86 days of flow they lost; see research/2026-10/gaps/forced_loss_r52-notes.md

not_counted.lukoil_transit_2024: Ukraine's sanctions stopped Lukoil's crude through Druzhba to Hungary and Slovakia from 18 July 2024; other Russian suppliers (Tatneft, Russneft) took over and MOL took title at the Belarus-Ukraine border from September. No measured loss of volume; not counted.
not_counted.gas_transit_2025: Ukraine ended Russian gas transit on 1 January 2025 (Slovakia, Austria, Moldova). Already shown as gas Russia's supply stopped ('without the gas Russia cut off itself', RUSSIA_GAS_CUT); not a baseline change this round.
not_counted.food_bans: Russia's grain export ban to the EAEU (March-June 2022), its sugar ban (March-August 2022) and its rice ban (from July 2023) are sudden export bans too; they fall on goods the build does not split by product, so they are not counted. Left for a decision.
